#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --account=m4138
#SBATCH --constraint=gpu
#SBATCH --qos=regular
#SBATCH --time=01:00:00
#SBATCH --nodes=2
#SBATCH --gpus-per-node=4

cd /pscratch/sd/z/zjia//nccl-tests
module load cray-mpich/8.1.25
# nccl/2.15.5-ofi
module load nccl
# cudatoolkit/11.7
module load cudatoolkit
conda activate qs

export MPICH_GPU_SUPPORT_ENABLED=1
# make MPI=1 MPI_HOME=$CRAY_MPICH_DIR CUDA_HOME=/opt/nvidia/hpc_sdk/Linux_x86_64/22.7/cuda/11.7 NCCL_HOME=/global/common/software/nersc/pm-2022q4/sw/nccl-2.15.5-ofi-r4
GPUSPERNODE=4
srun -u \
     --ntasks="$(( SLURM_JOB_NUM_NODES ))" \
     --ntasks-per-node=1 \
     ./build/alltoall_perf -b 4G -e 4G -f 2 -d double -g ${GPUSPERNODE} -w 0 -n 10 > nccl-2nodes.log

issues: The `cd` command uses a double slash `//` in the path `/pscratch/sd/z/zjia//nccl-tests`. While this typically resolves correctly on Unix-like systems, it is unconventional and could be cleaned up to use a single slash.

The variable `GPUSPERNODE` is hardcoded to 4. This correctly matches the `--gpus-per-node=4` SBATCH directive in this specific script. However, this creates a potential point of failure if the SBATCH directive is changed without updating the variable. A more robust approach would be to use a Slurm environment variable (e.g., `$SLURM_GPUS_ON_NODE`) to ensure consistency.
